title: RECKLESS HOMICIDE
full_story:
Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip M. Givens announced that William K. Shufeldt, 45, of Iuka, was sentenced to time in the Illinois Department of Corrections on Wednesday, in Clay County Circuit Court for the offense of Reckless Homicide, a Class 3 Felony.

The charge alleged that on September 27, 2024, Shufeldt, while acting in a reckless manner, performed acts causing the death of the victim, 59-year-old Mia S. Daniels from Monticello, AR, in that he drove at an excessive speed greater than was reasonable and proper to the existing traffic conditions and the safety of persons properly upon the roadway.  Shufeldt pled guilty to the offense on January 7th.  He was sentenced to the maximum of 5 years to the Illinois Department of Corrections Wednesday.  Shufeldt will have a 6-month period of Mandatory Supervised Release.

The investigation was conducted by the Illinois State Police and the Clay County Sheriff’s Office.  State Police said Shufeldt was attempting to pass other vehicles including a semi while eastbound on US 50 near the Xenia-Iola Road and struck the Daniels vehicle head-on.

State’s Attorney Phillip Givens said: “My heart goes out to the family in this case.  They lost their mother, grandmother, sister, aunt, and friend.  The fact that the maximum sentence is only 5 years when a life was lost is sad.  I am grateful for the investigation in this case and the best possible outcome as my office continues to work with law enforcement to hold people accountable for their actions.”

title: EFFINGHAM ARREST
full_story:
An Effingham man is in custody after his arrest Monday for various drug offenses.

38-year-old Allen G. Matlock was taken into custody for delivery of 15 to 100 grams of methamphetamine, possession of 15 to 100 grams of meth, delivery of 50 to 200 grams of controlled substance, manufacture of 400 to 900 grams of a controlled substance, and possession of 400 to 900 grams of a controlled substance.

On Monday, investigators from the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office, the Effingham City Police Department, and the Drug Enforcement Administration were assisted by the ILEAS Special Response Team in executing a search warrant at 108 South Willow in Effingham.

The search warrant was the result of a joint narcotics investigation conducted by the Sheriff’s Office, Police Department, and Drug Enforcement Administration.

Execution of the warrant resulted in the seizure of a substantial amount of crystal methamphetamine, psilocybin mushrooms, a DMT (Dimethyltryptamine) extraction laboratory, a large quantity of DMT, and other controlled substances.  Additionally, investigators located evidence consistent with the manufacture and distribution of narcotics.

The Effingham County sheriff’s office, Effingham police department, and DEA were assisted at the scene by the Effingham Fire Department and the Illinois State Police Clandestine Laboratory Response Team.

title: BRIDGE REPLACEMENT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation announced the closure of Old US 50 between Cedar Elm Drive and Country Road 800 E for a bridge replacement project over Raccoon Creek.  Work is expected to begin Monday, March 16th, and be completed by August.

A detour will be posted directing traffic to use U.S. 50 between Xenia and Flora.  This project will improve safety and the smoothness of the pavement along Old US 50 for the traveling public.

Motorists will need to follow the posted detour or find an alternate route.  Drivers should allow extra time for trips through this area, pay close attention to changed conditions and obey the posted speed limits.

title: FARINA COUPLE DIES
full_story:
A Farina couple died from injuries sustained in a February 19th crash on I-57 south near the Edgewood intersection in Effingham County.

76-year-old James Rentfro, who was the driver, died on March 3rd.  His wife, Catherine Rentfrow, died on March 7th.

State Police say James Rentfrow was the driver of an SUV that was struck in the rear by a semi.  Catherine was a passenger.  The impact then pushed the Rentfrow vehicle into a car in front of it.

The driver of the truck, 61-year-old Mark Lawson of Dallas, Texas, was issued a citation for failure to reduce speed to avoid an accident.  He was not injured.

James Rentfrow was a dairy farmer who formerly lived in Effingham.  He and his wife were both involved in Campers on a Mission, an organization of evangelical Christian campers and RVers dedicated to sharing their faith and love for Jesus through various missions.

title: MITIGATION PLANNING COMMITTEE MEETING
full_story:
The Clay County Hazard Mitigation Planning Committee will hold its first meeting on Wednesday, March 18th, at 1:00 PM.  The meeting will be at the Clay County Health Department and is open to the public.

Clay County will update its hazard mitigation plan to reduce the damages caused by severe weather such as thunderstorms, floods, snow and ice storms, and tornados, among other events.  This plan and the process to update it will be funded through a grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).

“The Plan describes the natural hazard events that have impacted the County and identifies activities and projects to reduce the risk to our residents and infrastructure,” said Steve Lewis, Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency Coordinator.  “By having an updated hazard mitigation plan, the County and its participating jurisdictions will remain eligible for federal funds to carry out these projects and activities,” he added.

The Planning Committee includes representatives from the County, their municipalities, townships, school districts, fire protection districts, and healthcare services, as well as technical partners and other stakeholders.  Meetings of this committee will be conducted over the next year as working sessions so that any interested residents can attend and ask questions.  The purpose of these working sessions is to gather and discuss information that will be used to update the Plan.

Lewis added, “This mitigation plan is different from our County’s emergency response plan because it focuses on ways to reduce and prevent damages before they occur.”

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Noble Village Board met in regular session Monday evening.

Mayor Brad Kessler announced with a heavy heart the unexpected passing of Mike Bridges of Charleston Engineering.  He noted Mike’s long-standing work with the Village and expressed condolences.  The mayor further reported that representatives from Charleston Engineering met with him and confirmed that Paul and Brandon will be handling the Village’s account moving forward.  Mayor Kessler said that Paul Muhs, with Charleston Engineering, will be reaching out to Enlow Inc. and let them know that they can start the Cherry/Palmer Street drainage project.

The Village received an OSHA Inspection Citation and Notification of Penalty.  All required corrective actions have been completed with the exception of the hazardous materials training and fire extinguisher training.  A hazardous materials training class is scheduled for Wednesday.  Mayor Brad Kessler will be reaching out to Jake Anderson to arrange the necessary training for the fire extinguishers for the Village employees.

Residents were reminded that ground decorations at the Noble Cemetery need to be removed by March 31st.  Remaining ground decorations after the 31st will be disposed of by village employees.  Village of Noble Clean-up Day is scheduled for April 29th.

The next village board meeting is set for March 23rd, at 7:00 pm.

title: WEATHER SPOTTER TRAINING
full_story:
The National Weather Service is offering their annual severe weather spotter training on Thursday, March 19th at 6:00 pm.  The class will be held at Frontier Community College.

Severe storm spotters are a VITAL part of the severe weather warning process.  Spotters provide critical, and potentially, lifesaving information to their communities and surrounding locations – and to National Weather Service (NWS) forecasters who are using these reports to help issue warnings and keep the public updated during severe weather events.

The in-person training covers severe weather hazards including thunderstorms and tornadoes, safety concerns, planning for and anticipating severe thunderstorms, general storm structure and movement, and identification of important storm features.

This year’s program offers more interactive portions of the sessions.  The session will last about 2 hours and are free and open to the public.  Registration is required and is available at wewather.gov/pah/spottertraining or scan the QR Code on the event flyers.

title: DICKERSON TO PERFORM
full_story:
The Du Quoin State Fair is proud to announce that country star Russell Dickerson will take the Grandstand stage on Saturday, September 5th, bringing his high-energy, feel-good country hits to one of Southern Illinois’ biggest summer traditions.

As a multi-Platinum headliner, Dickerson has spent the past decade carving out a unique space in country music.  With an exponentially growing fan base and a reputation for electric live performances, he continues to build momentum with the release of his fourth studio album, Famous Back Home.  Blending the heartfelt authenticity fans have always embraced with a fresh surge of raw, arena-ready energy, Famous Back Home captures Dickerson in full stride.  The album reflects both the tender family man and the dynamic showman fans experience on stage night after night.

“When we’re building a lineup, we look for artists who translate their music into a truly great live experience,” said Illinois Department of Agriculture Director Jerry Costello II.  “Russell Dickerson delivers an energy on stage that makes him a great fit for a Saturday night at the fair.”

Dickerson’s impressive run includes six No. 1 singles: “Yours” (3X Platinum), “Blue Tacoma” (2X Platinum), “Every Little Thing” (Platinum), “Love You Like I Used To” (2X Platinum), “God Gave Me a Girl,” and “Happen To Me” (Platinum).  His playful, 2X Platinum collaboration “She Likes It (with Jake Scott)” further cemented his reputation for upbeat, relatable storytelling, helping drive more than three billion career streams.

“Russell brings a modern country sound that’s upbeat, fun, and made for a live audience,” said Du Quoin State Fair Manager Luke Davison.  “This is the kind of show fairgoers look forward to all year, and we’re proud to add him to the 2026 lineup.”

Tickets for the Russell Dickerson concert will be available on Friday, beginning at 10 am via Ticketmaster.  Tier 3 tickets are $35, Tier 2 tickets are $45, and Tier 1 tickets are $55.  The Du Quoin State Fair runs from August 28th through September 7th.  To learn more, visit dsf.illinois.gov/.
